content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_8c1d0bca1d1d5fde4c5008\", \"title\": \"ZM3D playable: hand-off notes\", \"name\": \"ZM3D playable: hand-off notes\", \"revisionId\": \"5ddbee1c86\", \"createdTime\": \"2025-09-30T16:25:41Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2025-09-30T16:58:19Z\", \"text\": \"ZM3D playable: hand-off notes\\n\\nThe brief. One doc PlayableX can build from: which scenario we picked and what it is for, the eight items on the board and that every other board item on the list is an extra they can swap in, the four zombies and the one animation, how a level is won and lost and how many slots the tray has, what they can use for sound and when the music may start, and the start date. How the level plays is on the design page; your deck of the reference level has what we built for them. What they told us about formats still holds, and so does their rule from last time about when the music may start.\\n\\nThe hand-off list. One row per line of Brian's pack list, with these columns: Line, Category, Board set, State, What's owed, Who has it, Ticket. Line, Category and Ticket are as on his list. Board set is Default for the eight on the board and Extra for every other board item; leave it empty for anything that isn't a board item.\\n\\nState is one of three words, nothing else. Delivered: PlayableX has the current file and can use it. Ready: exported in a format they take and sitting in the outgoing folder, it opens, it is the current version and nobody is changing it. Owed: anything else. For an Owed line say what is owed, and who has it, meaning whoever has to do the next thing.\\n\\nBrian's note on each ticket says what he did with the line. Take it as it stands unless something later says otherwise, and go by how things stand today, not the day he wrote it: if someone who knows the file or the art has said something since, that counts. If the art changed after a file went out or was exported (a fix, a retexture, new colour versions), it goes again, and it sits with whoever the file came from.\\n\\nSound: we only hand over what is ours to hand over. Anything from a library or a bought pack stays here until we have our own version.\\n\\nTickets live under Brian's pack ticket, one per line. {"documentId": "f_8c1d0bca1d1d5fde4c5008", "title": "ZM3D playable: hand-off notes", "name": "ZM3D playable: hand-off notes", "revisionId": "5ddbee1c86", "createdTime": "2025-09-30T16:25:41Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-30T16:58:19Z", "text": "ZM3D playable: hand-off notes

The brief. One doc PlayableX can build from: which scenario we picked and what it is for, the eight items on the board and that every other board item on the list is an extra they can swap in, the four zombies and the one animation, how a level is won and lost and how many slots the tray has, what they can use for sound and when the music may start, and the start date. How the level plays is on the design page; your deck of the reference level has what we built for them. What they told us about formats still holds, and so does their rule from last time about when the music may start.

The hand-off list. One row per line of Brian's pack list, with these columns: Line, Category, Board set, State, What's owed, Who has it, Ticket. Line, Category and Ticket are as on his list. Board set is Default for the eight on the board and Extra for every other board item; leave it empty for anything that isn't a board item.

State is one of three words, nothing else. Delivered: PlayableX has the current file and can use it. Ready: exported in a format they take and sitting in the outgoing folder, it opens, it is the current version and nobody is changing it. Owed: anything else. For an Owed line say what is owed, and who has it, meaning whoever has to do the next thing.

Brian's note on each ticket says what he did with the line. Take it as it stands unless something later says otherwise, and go by how things stand today, not the day he wrote it: if someone who knows the file or the art has said something since, that counts. If the art changed after a file went out or was exported (a fix, a retexture, new colour versions), it goes again, and it sits with whoever the file came from.

Sound: we only hand over what is ours to hand over. Anything from a library or a bought pack stays here until we have our own version.

Tickets live under Brian's pack ticket, one per line. An Owed line's ticket goes to Todo with a comment saying what is owed and who has it. Leave the Delivered and Ready ones as they are.

Sharing: both files, view only. Everyone on the kickoff hold, and PlayableX through their intake address, which is in Contacts.
"}

{"ts": "1758911910.876289", "type": "message", "text": "I’ve been playing Archero 2 and <http://Survivor.io|Survivor.io> for a while, and I’ve developed some theories about how levels and monsters work in these games
• In Archero 2, the Arena usually uses a fixed set of monster types. These monsters are presented to the player in different sequences, creating variation across levels. I believe the game also adjusts level design based on the player’s current power-ups or skills. For example, if your build makes you stronger while standing still, you’re more likely to face levels that force you to move and kite enemies. Still, most levels seem to follow certain predefined monster patterns.
    ◦ Another thing I’m confident about is that the monsters’ HP, defense, and attack stats increase as you progress. A monster you encounter at Level 1 will appear again at Level 45, but with boosted stats. This scaling seems to be the game’s way of balancing the player’s increasing strength.
• In <http://Survivor.io|Survivor.io>, I don’t think monsters’ individual stats scale the same way. Instead, the difficulty comes from changes in camera zoom, monster variety, and, most importantly, quantity. The pool of monster types stays fairly limited, but the numbers ramp up dramatically. For instance, the same type of monster that spawns at the 0-minute mark might still appear at 6 minutes, but instead of 10 showing up, you’re suddenly dealing with 100. 2025-09-29T20:16:23Z Robert 1759176983.189479 rc= 1 : I think we should think about what 0.3.22 had and what we're keeping. | • Blunder was fine the way it is, but it got skewed because of these recent weird bot like behavior. | • Win rate still has more impact on funnel, blunder seems to be OK as long as people win. | • We are leaning more hardcore because casual doesn't cut it, or so we think | • We support this hardcore transition with level templates and monster scaling using a math formula | • We differentiate our game with the zombie killing + card mechanic | • Our live ops are fine since leaderboards/quests are standard in all RPGs. We have 2 modes catered towards this game. Plague Race is meh for hardcore but it's not going to make peop
2025-09-29T19:22:58Z Julia Lawson 1759173778.362129 rc= 1 : Very well, in that case, from now on if someone complains a level is "too hard" I'll just ignore them :smile:
2025-09-29T19:21:43Z Vincent Parker 1759173703.509829 rc= 0 : If we can go with zombie scaling then I agree wth levels being mid core or not casual
2025-09-29T19:21:38Z Julia Lawson 1759173698.236239 rc= 2 : For one thing we'd make the levels so that they would have deck building blocks and not put the baseline at CPM and win streak free win.
2025-09-29T19:21:33Z Brian Foster 1759173693.774649 rc= 0 : But given the current situation, since we’re not getting good performance from a casual game, I assume we’re considering shifting towards a more hardcore game as an alternative
2025-09-29T19:21:24Z Brian Foster 1759173684.934029 rc= 0 : Personally, I’ve never supported a hardcore match-3D game. With the current gameplay, I just can’t picture a hardcore game in my mind, but it's just me
2025-09-29T19:21:07Z Leonard Hayes 1759173667.736069 rc= 0 : to me your levels are perfectly fine <@EMPLOYEE_0005_SLACK_ID> :slightly_smiling_face:
2025-09-29T19:20:37Z Leonard Hayes 1759173637.851689 rc= 3 : I think levels have not much to do with item progression and effects after they are introduced earlier in the funnel. I don’t even know what a hardcore level looks like
2025-09-29T19:20:32Z Julia Lawson 1759173632.306909 rc= 0 : If you're confident we should yolo, it's just one test and one level swap, cheaper then A/B
2025-09-29T19:19:21Z Julia Lawson 1759173561.454829 rc= 4 : Needless to mention, I have 300 casual levels and nothing geared to midcore play
2025-09-29T19:19:20Z Leonard Hayes 1759173560.112239 rc= 0 : how much additional work is it to A/B test the hardcore funnel if we don’t want to yolo?
2025-09-29T19:18:29Z Julia Lawson 1759173509.076179 rc= 0 : We never had a preference between casual or midcore, it was upto you guys. We're just reminding that we're doing multiple things for multiple targets.
2025-09-29T19:18:19Z Robert 1759173499.498579 rc= 0 : D0 minutes at the expense of possibly an uglier funnel
2025-09-29T19:17:52Z Robert 1759173472.928899 rc= 0 : yeah, I thought we're leaning into hardcore too
2025-09-29T19:17:39Z Leonard Hayes 1759173459.621579 rc= 0 : I thought you guys all wanted to lean into hardcore - maybe I’m misreading what we wanted to do - now you guys are confusing me :smile:
2025-09-29T19:17:37Z Robert 1759173457.020249 rc= 0 : yeah, [USERNAME_15751] is not a casual/hardcore live ops, and we have boss arena/endless mode/leaderboards/quests, those are all standard..
2025-09-29T19:17:34Z Brian Foster 1759173454.898559 rc= 0 : That’s why I think we need a clear direction on this. Either we make a game for hardcore players and design the whole game accordingly, or we follow the casual path. Of course, I don’t think they’ll rage quit because of the live-ops
2025-09-29T19:16:29Z Vincent Parker 1759173389.051889 rc= 0 : The only casual live ops implemented is plague race [USERNAME_44360]. Quests can be more all around. The level progression and the boosts are also casual
2025-09-29T19:16:26Z Julia Lawson 1759173386.589489 rc= 0 : Yeah, I agree with [PERSON_NAME_0092]. We decided on a casual approach because liveops engine was going to be the backbone of the fundraising. I'm fine with iterating, obviously but but I don't understand why we're doing it for the hardcore players.
2025-09-29T19:14:30Z Brian Foster 1759173270.565169 rc= 0 : In the past, when making decisions on this, we chose a more casual approach since we were going to showcase our 'live-ops engine' for fundraising
2025-09-29T19:14:29Z Leonard Hayes 1759173269.820649 rc= 0 : Do we think the hardcore players will be turned off by the casual liveops structures? I’m thinking they will choose not to be engaged much with those features but I don’t think they will rage quit the game because There is a win streak liveops
2025-09-29T19:14:07Z Julia Lawson 1759173247.603649 rc= 0 : Also, you need to make the level ordering again. Before I did it manually but now we probably need some sort of script for it.

{"result":"{\"id\": \"page_zm3d_gdd\", \"space_id\": \"space_PROD\", \"parent_id\": \"page_prod_home\", \"title\": \"Zombie Match 3D \\u2014 Game Design Document\", \"body\": \"

This is the living Game Design Document for Zombie Match 3D (shipped on the store as Puzzles vs Zombies under Calm Play LLC until the transfer to Harmony Games and the rename on 24 July 2025). It is the source of truth for the core loop, the RPG combat layer, and monetization. For the coin/life economy see Economy Design - Coins, Lives & Boosters, and for the paid track see ZM3D Season Pass - Spec. This document ladders up to Product OKRs - 2025 H1.

ZM3D has not had a global launch. It first became publicly downloadable in the US on Google Play on April 12, 2025 and on the App Store on April 18, 2025; May 15, 2025 is the day iOS build 1.0.5 went live. This GDD reflects that build plus the Season Pass update.

Core mechanic

The matcher is a Match-3D collector benchmarked on Match Factory. Objects sit in a physics pile; the player drags items into a 7-slot tray. Collect any 3 matching objects and they clear from the tray. If all 7 slots fill without a match it counts as a blunder: the tray clears and surviving monsters enrage, but play continues. It is a tempo penalty, not a fail state - the loss screen only appears at zero health. Tray pressure is the primary difficulty dial.

  • Pile physics - objects settle and occlude each other; digging exposes buried matches.
  • 7-slot tray - the primary tempo penalty, not the fail state; tuning slot count changes felt difficulty more than object count.
  • Object families - cosmetic skins that map to elemental ammo in the RPG layer.

Zombie RPG layer

Levels wrap the matcher in combat. Each cleared triple fires the matching element at the current monster. Monsters carry an elemental weakness; hitting the weakness deals bonus damage and can apply a status.

Monster / element table

The roster is an everyday-people theme rather than classic undead. Minion families scale in tiers; bosses come in standard, Fast and Turbo variants.

FamilyTypeTiers
PunkMinion1-5
BikerMinion1-4
KarenMinion1-4
AfroMinion1-3
Riot Police, Chef, Scientist, Fire Fighter, Magician, Librarian, Tech Bro, Gym Bro, Baseball Player, CheerleaderMinionin development
VarC-Mayor1 250 / VarC-Mayor2 225 / VarC-Chef 175 (base HP, scaled at runtime; the older 180/300/500 prefabs are retired)Bossstandard, Fast, Turbo

Elemental weaknesses used by boosters and abilities: shock, poison, burn, freeze, splash, stun, blind. Glue is a booster, not an element.

Modes

  • Campaign - authored levels, escalating monster mixes.
  • Endless - survival board with an item refill every 30s to keep the pile stocked.
  • Infinite-HP Boss - a damage-race against a boss whose HP does not deplete to zero; the score is total damage dealt before the tray fills.

Monetization

The headline product is the Season Pass at $6.99, reached production in the week of September 22-29, 2025. It runs a free and a premium reward track over a fixed season window; progression is earned through campaign and Endless play. Coin, life, and booster sinks live in the linked Economy doc - do not duplicate values here.

Known launch issues (tracked, historical):

  • Hard crash from consecutive glass-impact SFX/VFX on Android, mostly Samsung (Aug-Sep 2025, ZOM-475), fixed by removing the glass SFX and VFX. The separate addressables splash-hang belongs to Domino Delights.
  • The font-download freeze that stalls the splash screen at ~22% on slow connections is also Domino Delights (ENG-2346, May 2025); the ZM3D client has no remote font download.

Boss mode reward config

Owner: Robert (Product). Design: Julia Lawson. Changes to tray count or refill cadence must be reviewed against the OKR dashboard before shipping.

{"result":"{\"id\": \"page_domino_gdd\", \"space_id\": \"space_PROD\", \"parent_id\": \"page_prod_home\", \"title\": \"Domino Delights \\u2014 Game Design Document\", \"body\": \"

Domino Delights (internal codename \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\" / GoD) is Harmony Games' tile-connecting puzzle title with light-RPG progression. This document is the living design reference for the core loop, character system, and retention mini-games. Store title is Domino Delights; use Game of Dominoes or GoD internally.

Built through the Baklava release train, which shipped 11 September 2024; the soft launch itself was the US go-live on 11 April 2025, worldwide on 6 May 2025. ~4,800 levels across 160 chapters are in production. This GDD supersedes the pre-soft-launch draft; see the version history for the edit trail.

Core Loop & Mechanics

Players match a face-up board tile against the tile in hand — tripeak-solitaire structure on domino tiles — drawing from the draw pile when nothing matches. Each unbroken match chain feeds a streak meter; sustained combos drive the light-RPG layer, where collected characters level up and unlock stronger board-clearing abilities. A single run alternates between board-clearing turns and character-ability triggers, keeping session length short but replayable across the ~4,800-level ladder.

Boosts

  • Magical Gust - a wind boost that clears all face-up tiles on the board, resetting a stalled position.
  • Character abilities (below) act as targeted boosts that recharge through matching.

For coin, life, and booster balancing that these mechanics feed into, see Economy Design - Coins, Lives & Boosters.

Characters

Four playable characters (Sophie is the starter, the other three are collectible), each with its own upgrade track. Leveling a character deepens its signature effect and reduces its recharge cost.

CharacterSignature abilityUpgrade track
SophieStarts unlocked. Adds tiles to the draw pile and turns tiles wildImproves draw quality and wild frequency
NathanRemoves a set of random face-up tiles; jumbo tile to handIncreases tiles removed per trigger and jumbo size
JuliusRemoves face-up tiles and converts them to gold or wildIncreases tiles converted per trigger
LexiForesight - reveals upcoming tilesExtends how far ahead she reveals

Wildcard is a booster, not a character.

Character names and the fifth slot are provisional. Do not surface upgrade numbers in marketing until the economy pass locks recharge costs.

Retention Mini-Games

Between level runs, players can enter reward mini-games that keep engagement high on off-days:

  • Tile Dozer - a coin-pusher where dropped tiles shove a stacked tray toward the edge for coin and booster payouts.
  • Lucky Drop - a drop-and-bounce board awarding tiered rewards by landing slot (prototyped as \\\"Plinko\\\"; renamed for trademark reasons before ship).
  • River Tile - a timed matching mini-game (prototyped as \\\"Conveyor Belt\\\").
  • Memory Game - a pairs game on a timer.

Reward scaling for Tile Dozer and the other mini-games is tuned to daily-return targets and shares the coin sink with the core economy.

Competitive Context

Positioning benchmarks against the tile-matching leader are tracked in Competitive Analysis - Match Factory.

{"id": "page_domino_gdd", "space_id": "space_PROD", "parent_id": "page_prod_home", "title": "Domino Delights \u2014 Game Design Document", "body": "

Domino Delights (internal codename \"Game of Dominoes\" / GoD) is Harmony Games' tile-connecting puzzle title with light-RPG progression. This document is the living design reference for the core loop, character system, and retention mini-games. Store title is Domino Delights; use Game of Dominoes or GoD internally.

Built through the Baklava release train, which shipped 11 September 2024; the soft launch itself was the US go-live on 11 April 2025, worldwide on 6 May 2025. ~4,800 levels across 160 chapters are in production. This GDD supersedes the pre-soft-launch draft; see the version history for the edit trail.

Core Loop & Mechanics

Players match a face-up board tile against the tile in hand — tripeak-solitaire structure on domino tiles — drawing from the draw pile when nothing matches. Each unbroken match chain feeds a streak meter; sustained combos drive the light-RPG layer, where collected characters level up and unlock stronger board-clearing abilities. A single run alternates between board-clearing turns and character-ability triggers, keeping session length short but replayable across the ~4,800-level ladder.

Boosts

  • Magical Gust - a wind boost that clears all face-up tiles on the board, resetting a stalled position.
  • Character abilities (below) act as targeted boosts that recharge through matching.

For coin, life, and booster balancing that these mechanics feed into, see Economy Design - Coins, Lives & Boosters.

Characters

Four playable characters (Sophie is the starter, the other three are collectible), each with its own upgrade track. Leveling a character deepens its signature effect and reduces its recharge cost.

CharacterSignature abilityUpgrade track
SophieStarts unlocked. Adds tiles to the draw pile and turns tiles wildImproves draw quality and wild frequency
NathanRemoves a set of random face-up tiles; jumbo tile to handIncreases tiles removed per trigger and jumbo size
JuliusRemoves face-up tiles and converts them to gold or wildIncreases tiles converted per trigger
LexiForesight - reveals upcoming tilesExtends how far ahead she reveals

Wildcard is a booster, not a character.

Character names and the fifth slot are provisional. Do not surface upgrade numbers in marketing until the economy pass locks recharge costs.

Retention Mini-Games

Between level runs, players can enter reward mini-games that keep engagement high on off-days:

  • Tile Dozer - a coin-pusher where dropped tiles shove a stacked tray toward the edge for coin and booster payouts.
  • Lucky Drop - a drop-and-bounce board awarding tiered rewards by landing slot (prototyped as \"Plinko\"; renamed for trademark reasons before ship).
  • River Tile - a timed matching mini-game (prototyped as \"Conveyor Belt\").
  • Memory Game - a pairs game on a timer.

Reward scaling for Tile Dozer and the other mini-games is tuned to daily-return targets and shares the coin sink with the core economy.

Competitive Context

Positioning benchmarks against the tile-matching leader are tracked in Competitive Analysis - Match Factory.

The Gist
Team discusses upcoming projects, sales tax, game mechanics, gold tiles, rewind button, dynamite tiles, workload, and goals to ensure successful completion of projects and avoid burnout.

Action Items
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to check if sales tax is charged for subscription software purchases
• Arthur to check if sales tax is charged for Figma subscription
• Arthur to run Unity seat licenses through [PERSON_NAME_0054]’ card to avoid sales tax
• Leonard to break down Figma pages into multiple pages for easier navigation
• Arthur to close out the family and friends build by the end of the day
• Leonard to aim for the end of the first week of October for the next family and friends build
• Arthur to create tickets for various tasks related to the family and friends build
• [PERSON_NAME_0029] to limit the wildcard to one per row in the game
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to make a minor change to the game rules to allow for either one wildcard or one redemption tile per row, or one of each.
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to clarify the logic behind the calculation of the number of tiles per row.
• Leonard to adjust the percentage for gold tiles to increase the number of goals.
• [PERSON_NAME_0029] to share the details about how things are calculated with [PERSON_NAME_0054].
• [PERSON_NAME_0099] to focus on low-hanging fruit tasks and not work on the rewind feature.
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to hide the rewind button for the family and friends build.
• Arthur to help [PERSON_NAME_0099] figure out how to handle the collision issue with dynamite tiles.
• [PERSON_NAME_0099] to try flagging the tiles affected by dynamite explosions and figure out how to handle the collision issue.
• [PERSON_NAME_0099] to fix the bug found by [PERSON_NAME_97912] [PERSON_NAME_0099] to work on the rewind feature and address the issues with the bomb tile
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to test the rewind feature and its impact on streak bonuses
• Leonard to gather feedback from the team on the additional stress and workload caused by the family and friends build Push
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to discuss with [PERSON_NAME_5466] on how to assess scenarios like the friends and family build
• Leonard to ensure functional aspects of the friends and family build meet the quality bar
• Leonard to provide a better context and set expectations before starting a project
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] and Leonard to deliver an even better version of the build by the upcoming Friday
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to have a conversation with the team about overworking and the potential risks of burnout
• Leonard to encourage team members to take vacations and have conversations about workload management
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to share his experiences with managing individuals who struggle with workload management
• Leonard to take more vacations and encourage others to do the same
• Team to have conversations about workload planning and overcommunication to prevent overdrives
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to thank the team for their input and feedback during the postmortem meeting
Status Update By Topic
• Sales Tax: Discussed the possibility of sales tax being charged for subscription software and physical goods, with [PERSON_NAME_0054] noting that he can buy things for the company to avoid sales tax.
• Wildcard Tiles: Discussed the current restriction of one wildcard or redemption tile per row, with [PERSON_NAME_0054] proposing a change to allow one wildcard and one redemption tile per row.
• Family and Friends Build: Agreed to aim for the end of the first week of October to have the build ready for the board meeting.
• Ticket Creation: Agreed to create tickets for the family and friends stuff, with Arthur noting that they need to close it out today.
• Glow Effect: Discussed the glow effect for pieces revealed via wildcard, with Leonard noting that it was nice to have but not a priority.
• Darkening Water: Discussed the mini game darkening water, with Leonard noting that it was hard to see on the iPhone.
• Bill Check: Discussed checking the bill from today, with Arthur noting that they built up a few hours ago.
• Calculation Logic: The team discussed the logic behind the calculation of the number of tiles per row. They determined that it is not a simple 25% equal chance per number, as the probability of rolling a seven on two dice is higher than rolling ones and twelves.
• UI: [PERSON_NAME_0029] is working on the UI part for the shop, and [PERSON_NAME_0099] is focusing on the long hair, low hanging fruits upon attack, take rewind. [PERSON_NAME_5466] suggested hiding the rewind button for the family and friends build.
• Dynamite Tiles: Dynamite tiles are causing issues as they are competing to remove the same piece off the board. [PERSON_NAME_5466] suggested flagging them or setting a state to sort through the affected tiles. [PERSON_NAME_0099] is working on the bug and will try [PERSON_NAME_5466]’s suggestion.
• Rewind: Rewind is proving to be difficult as it requires a lot of things to be done. [PERSON_NAME_5466] suggested flagging or setting a state to mark the affected tiles. [PERSON_NAME_0099] is working on the bug and will try [PERSON_NAME_5466]’s suggestion.
• Rewind Feature: The team discussed the edge cases and stipulations of the rewind feature, such as the wild card bonus in Domino Dreams, and the fact that rewinding the last piece does not remove the streak effect.
• Family and Friends Build Push: The team discussed the impact of the Push on the engineering team, and the importance of setting clear goals and timelines to avoid overworking and cramming new things at the last minute.
• Optimization: The team discussed the need to set aside time for optimization and tuning when introducing new assets.
• Silver Bullet Philosophy: The team discussed the importance of understanding the true importance of a goal to the business and how to articulate it to the team.
• Asian Engineering: The team discussed the common experience of [NATIONALITY_2601] engineers not communicating their struggles and how to manage their workload.
• Quality Bar: The team discussed the importance of setting a quality bar for the work and how to ensure it is met.
• Overdrive: The team discussed the importance of avoiding overdrive and burnout and how to manage workloads.
• Vacations: The team discussed the importance of taking vacations and how to encourage it.

    ◦ The sound that plays when a bomb explodes.

    ◦ The sound that plays when our character adds a new tile to the deck. Should be *remotely changeable.*

• *Draw Tile from Deck*

import csv,io,json
src=open('/tmp/s/pack.csv').read()
rows=list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(src)))
default={"Grenade","Couch","Plushie Chick","Shuriken","Cute Axe","Gift Box","Cactus Plant","Bow"}
delivered={"Couch","Couch and Pillow","Grenade","Plushie Bunny","Plushie Chick","Cannon","Background","Zombie characters"}
owed={
 "Propane Tank":("FBX export (not exported yet)","Brian"),

 "Rubber Ducky":("FBX from Claire, then export","Claire"),
 "Grand Piano":("FBX from Claire, then export","Claire"),

 "Chainsaw":("Re-export FBX: new colour versions made after the 25 Sep export (Robert, 29 Sep)","Claire"),
 "Cone":("Re-export FBX: new colour versions made after the 25 Sep export (Robert, 29 Sep)","Claire"),
 "Rocket sound":("Our own rocket sound: current one is from the Soundly library and can't be handed over","Calvin"),

 "Background music":("Ad track cut down to a loop, exported as .wav/.mp3","Calvin"),
 "Item visuals":("Item icons pulled from Figma as PNG","Brian"),
 "UI elements":("UI pulled from Figma as PNG","Brian"),
 "Fonts":(".ttf files","Martin"),
}
out=[["Line","Category","Board set","State","What's owed","Who has it","Ticket"]]
cnt={}
for r in rows:
  l=r["Line"]
  bs="" if r["Kind"]!="Board item" else ("Default" if l in default else "Extra")
  if l in delivered: st,w,who="Delivered","",""
  elif l in owed: st="Owed"; w,who=owed[l]
  else: st,w,who="Ready","",""
  cnt[st]=cnt.get(st,0)+1
  out.append([l,r["Category"],bs,st,w,who,r["Ticket"]])
assert len(out)==97
assert sum(1 for o in out if o[2]=="Default")==8
json.dump(out,open('/tmp/s/out.json','w'))
print(cnt)
print([o[6] for o in out if o[3]=="Owed"])
EOF

input.title: ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX
input.bodyText:
ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX
Zombie Match 3D (Puzzles vs Zombies) | Harmony Games | prepared by Julia Lawson, 1 Oct 2025

This brief covers the game as it plays today. Frederick has flagged that a core gameplay change is under consideration. If the core changes, we will redo the affected parts of this brief with you in November.

1. Start date
Kickoff and build start: Monday 3 November 2025 (the new date you are holding for us). We are aiming to have every file still owed (see the hand-off list) with you before then.

2. Scenario
We picked Scenario 1, the core game mechanic. What it is for: retention, not cheapest CPI. The aim is to filter out players who won't like the game, while staying true to the core gameplay, so test results reflect the real game. The player picks items freely and can make several matches if they're good enough; it is not on rails.

3. How a level plays (from the ZM3D design page and our reference level)
- Items sit in a physics pile on the board. The player drags items into a tray at the bottom.
- The tray has 7 slots. Any 3 matching items in the tray clear and fire at the zombies.
- Different items hit zombies differently (e.g. Grenade = powerful, Couch = splash damage, plushie = weak but funny).
- If all 7 slots fill without a match, that is a blunder: the tray clears and the zombies get enraged, but play carries on. A blunder is a tempo penalty, not a loss.
- Win: every zombie on screen is eliminated.
- Lose: the zombies reach us and our HP runs out.
Reference: Brian's recorded reference level (video shared in the channel on 24 Sep) and our deck "ZM3D playable - reference level" show what we built for you.

4. Board items: the 8 on the board
Grenade, Couch, Plushie Chick, Shuriken, Cute Axe, Gift Box, Cactus Plant, Bow.
(Grenade, Couch and Plushie Chick come from the reference level. Bow replaced Dynamite in the 8. The Bow goes in as it is now; an arrow may come later as its own item.)
Every other board item on the hand-off list is an extra that you can swap in through the editable board, Dynamite included.

5. Zombies and animation
- Four zombies: Party Girl, Plumber, Magician, Football Player. All four are in the Unity package Marcus sent on 26 Sep.
- One animation: walk. Please apply it to all four when you re-rig them in Spine.
- We may add more zombies later, depending on size.

6. Sound and music
- You can use these sounds: Matching, Success and Failure (made in-house), plus the background music (a new ad track made in-house, not the in-game track).
- The Rocket and Explosion sounds currently in the game come from a library and a bought pack, so we can't hand them over. Calvin is making our own versions; they are owed on the hand-off list.
- Music: as per your rule from last time, the music may only start after the player's first click.

7. Formats (as you gave them to us; these still hold)
- 3D: .fbx (Binary, not ASCII), .glb or .blend
- 2D: .png (2D animations need character parts separated into pieces)
- Font: .ttf or .woff2
- Sound: .mp3 or .wav

8. What is still coming from us
The hand-off list sheet ("ZM3D playable - hand-off list") has one row per asset. Each row shows its state (Delivered / Ready / Owed), what is still owed and who has it. As of 1 Oct: 8 Delivered, 68 Ready, 20 Owed.
- Delivered: you have the current file and can use it.
- Ready: exported in a format you take and sitting in our outgoing folder. It opens, it's the current version and nobody is changing it.
- Owed: everything else.

Hi PlayableX team! Ahead of the 3 November start, here's the brief to build from and our hand-off list:
• Brief: https://docs.google.com/document/d/8505dd1432aa4998b4b74087/edit
• Hand-off list: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1g2aY3O7AfSz4XXKvmAy2dXdG35_Ll5C8uT0iQoSkxds/edit

Both are shared view-only with intake@playablex.ai.

The hand-off list has one row per asset, marked Delivered, Ready (exported and waiting to go out to you) or Owed. Owed rows say what's still coming from us. As of today, 20 items are still owed. These include a re-export of the Cactus Plant (one of the 8 board items), our own rocket and explosion sounds, the background music loop, fonts, item icons and UI PNGs.

To answer your zombie question: please use one animation, walk, on Party Girl, Plumber, Magician and Football Player. All four are in the Unity package from 26 Sep.

The brief reflects the game as it is today. If the core changes, we'll go through the affected parts with you in November.

content.text:
I've done everything Frederick asked for: the brief and the hand-off list are in your Drive, the tickets are updated, Frederick has his counts, and both links are posted in the PlayableX channel.

**Item pack status (96 lines):**

| State | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Delivered | 8 | Couch, Couch and Pillow, Grenade, Plushie Bunny, Plushie Chick, Cannon, Background, Zombie characters |
| Ready | 68 | Exported in a format PlayableX takes and sitting in the outgoing folder |
| Owed | 20 | Claire 9, Brian 7, Calvin 3, Martin 1 |

**What changed from Brian's ticket notes:**
- **Board:** on Sep 26 Robert swapped the Bow into the 8 in place of Dynamite, so Dynamite is now an extra. The 8 are Grenade, Couch, Plushie Chick, Shuriken, Cute Axe, Gift Box, Cactus Plant and Bow.
- **Cactus, Chainsaw and Cone:** Robert posted new colour versions on Sep 29, after Claire's Sep 25 export. All three go back to Owed with Claire, and the Cactus is one of the 8.
- **Rocket and Explosion sounds:** Calvin's "ZM3D sound sources" sheet shows they come from the Soundly library and a bought Asset Store pack. Brian had exported them, but they stay with us as Owed until Calvin makes our own versions.
- **Zombies:** Robert picked Party Girl, Plumber, Magician and Football Player, with walk as the one animation. All four are in the Unity package Marcus put together, sent Sep 26.

**What I did:**
- **Brief doc** ("ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX"), written for the game as it is today:
  - Scenario 1 and why we picked it.
  - The 8 board items, with everything else as swap-in extras.
  - The 4 zombies and the walk animation.
  - Win and lose rules and the 7-slot tray, from the ZM3D design page.
  - Which sounds they can use, and their rule from the Dominoes playable that music only starts after the first click.
  - Their file formats and the Nov 3 start date.
- **Hand-off sheet** ("ZM3D playable - hand-off list"): one row per line of Brian's pack list, with the columns Frederick asked for.
- **Linear:** moved the 20 Owed tickets to Todo, each with a comment saying what's owed and who has it. I left the Delivered and Ready tickets as they were.
- **Sharing:** both files are view-only for Frederick, Brian and Robert (everyone on the Nov 3 kickoff hold) and for intake@playablex.ai from Contacts.
- **Slack:** sent Frederick the counts and the changes above in your DM, and posted both links in the PlayableX channel. That post lists what's still coming from us and gives them the zombie and animation picks they asked for on Sep 29.

**Brief:** https://docs.google.com/document/d/8505dd1432aa4998b4b74087/edit
**Hand-off list:** https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1g2aY3O7AfSz4XXKvmAy2dXdG35_Ll5C8uT0iQoSkxds/edit
